messages:
eve: Heads-up  I've uploaded a new frame for the autoscale panel that rejiggers visual hierarchy. Main ask: make min/max + current allocation the dominant read, demote SLO slider visually but keep it discoverable. Comments please.

matt: Quick reaction: agree that allocation numbers should jump out. Current mock uses large numeric display for current allocation which is good, but the SLO slider uses the same accent color which competes. Suggest using a muted color for the slider track and keep accent for the numbers only.

li: UX note: if we tone down the slider color, add a short descriptor line under it (e.g., "Latency SLO (median ms)") so users don't miss why it exists. Also consider a collapsed detail chevron for advanced SLO controls.

anika: On pool selection: the dropdown currently lists pool names only. People asked for a small subtitle with region + gpu type and a tiny tag if pool supports burst. Eg: "us-west-2 • A100" and a green dot + label "burst". That helps when switching.

eve: Good call. Also want to test an inline micro-sparkline near the allocation number to show recent utilization; that gives context for why someone might increase max. Keep sparkline tiny and monochrome so it doesn't draw attention away.

matt: Implementation: sparkline can be an SVG with aria-hidden=true; but we need an accessible label: "Recent CPU/GPU utilization: 32% avg" available on hover/focus via aria-describedby.

aria: Accessibility checklist: 1) Slider must expose role=slider and aria-valuetext with ms + short cost estimate, 2) Pool dropdown items should include accessible name combining pool label and attributes (region, gpu type, burst availability), 3) When capacity changes are applied, announce via aria-live polite: "Capacity updated: min 2, max 8, current 3".

li: Copy tweak: replace the ambiguous "Burst" label with "Burst cushion" and microcopy: "Temporary extra GPUs for short spikes. May incur extra cost." Keep the microcopy under the burst indicator.

anika: I prototyped two guardrail styles: (A) inline soft warning pill next to the stepper, (B) brief modal requiring checkbox override. Preference from research leans to (A) because modal halts flow. Pill should include "Why?" link to policy.

matt: Agreed for pill. One nuance: if user keeps trying to exceed hard cap after overriding, show a toast error and revert the change to avoid silent failures.

eve: Decision draft: 1) Visual hierarchy: big current allocation number + tiny sparkline, muted SLO slider with descriptor, 2) Pool dropdown shows region/gpu tag + burst badge, 3) "Burst cushion" naming + microcopy, 4) Guardrail = inline pill with "Why?" and accessible override checkbox, 5) Aria-live announcements on apply, sparkline aria-hidden but described. Assign: @li update copy, @anika update components in Figma, @matt add aria-live and toast behavior, @aria run a11y pass.

ops-bot: Created ticket AUTOSCALE-672: "Visual hierarchy + burst naming + guardrail pill" and assigned to li, anika, matt, aria.

aria: Quick aria suggestion for the pill: give it id="guardrail-pill" and use aria-describedby on the stepper: aria-describedby="guardrail-pill" so screen readers read the pill message when focusing the control. Also ensure color is not the only indicator.

eve: Thanks all. I'll update the prototype with the muted slider and sparkline tonight and share a short test link. If anyone has objections to the pill-first guardrail approach speak now, otherwise I'll mark this resolved. :white_check_mark:
